title: Shopping cart: stock, payment, and receipts
description: A synthetic reusable-bottle shop contrasts current checkout without a stock hold with a proposed reservation path, stock rejection, and payment retry. Wiring separates Angular actions, Spring endpoints, individual SQL operations, payment, SNS/SQS receipt delivery, and Datadog traces.
overview:
All actors, identifiers, endpoints, products, providers, SQL, telemetry, and work references are synthetic assumptions. The shared Wiring inventory describes interface ownership, not verified infrastructure, IAM, network access, or deployment boundaries. Amounts are integer euro cents; bottles cost 2450 cents and the examples assume tax is included and delivery is free.

Compare Current: authorization without a hold with the Proposed successful checkout. Current stops at payment authorization without checking stock. The proposal reserves stock first and assumes a five-minute hold remains valid during payment retry. Proposed recordings assume the target contracts work; missing/changed markers identify contract decisions still requiring work, not measured production availability. The DELETE release endpoint is an unexplored missing definition.

Each SQL SELECT, UPDATE, and INSERT has its own wire and database-owned port. Inventory hold creation assumes one transaction across the stock read, counter update, and hold insert; cross-store completion atomicity and crash recovery are outside this recording. After an order commit, SNS publication and SNS-to-SQS fan-out are recorded separately from later Lambda consumption. Assume raw SNS message delivery to SQS, at-least-once transport, and worker deduplication by eventId; this example does not establish those operational guarantees. Datadog receives synthetic OTLP traces through an assumed compatible ingestion boundary. No tokens, credentials, signed URLs, or personal payloads appear in telemetry.

Wiring relevance belongs to occurrence IDs, including revisits. Connections include only their endpoint owners and named ports; adjacent calls are never inferred. Local human review uses an explicit empty mapping. The retry's second review intentionally has no mapping recorded. Fictional CART-DEMO references describe work scope, not dependencies or progress.

comparisons.title: Available stock versus a stale basket
comparisons.description: The stock rejection stops before payment or receipt work. A visible payment capability on the shared map does not make it part of that recording.

comparisons.title: First authorization versus a new payment attempt
comparisons.description: The retry revisits reservation inspection and payment with distinct occurrence IDs. The accepted reservation is reused; the declined payment record remains captured beside the authorized attempt.

comparisons.title: Authorize immediately or hold stock first?
comparisons.description: Synthetic Current authorizes a two-bottle basket without a stock hold and stops at authorization. Proposed assumes Inventory accepts a hold before authorization and continues through receipt acceptance. These are authored recordings, not computed diffs or aligned steps.

components.label: Commerce records
components.description: Synthetic Amazon RDS PostgreSQL store. Each port describes one repository operation and its table columns; database records are independent of the Domain model.

operations.label: SELECT cart and lines
operations.statement: SELECT c.id, c.version, l.sku, l.quantity, c.total_minor FROM cart c JOIN cart_line l ON l.cart_id = c.id WHERE c.id = :cartId;

operations.label: UPDATE cart quantity
operations.statement: UPDATE cart_line SET quantity = :quantity WHERE cart_id = :cartId AND sku = :sku;
operations.description: Synthetic transaction also saves the server-priced total and cart version through separate UPDATE operations.

operations.label: UPDATE cart total and version
operations.statement: UPDATE cart SET total_minor = :totalMinor, version = version + 1 WHERE id = :cartId AND version = :expectedVersion;
operations.responses: One row updated; zero rows means CART_VERSION_CONFLICT

operations.label: INSERT payment attempt
operations.statement: INSERT INTO payment_attempt (id, cart_id, amount_minor, status) VALUES (:attemptId, :cartId, :amountMinor, :status);

operations.label: INSERT paid order
operations.statement: INSERT INTO purchase_order (id, cart_id, status, receipt_state) VALUES (:orderId, :cartId, 'paid', 'pending-publication');

fields.description: Proposed persistence gap; the illustrative INSERT still requires this column and binding decision.

operations.label: UPDATE receipt acceptance
operations.statement: UPDATE purchase_order SET receipt_state = 'accepted-by-provider' WHERE id = :orderId;

components.label: Inventory records
components.description: Synthetic Inventory-owned relational store. One transaction groups reservation reads and writes; lines remain separately inspectable.

operations.label: SELECT available stock FOR UPDATE
operations.statement: SELECT sku, on_hand_qty - reserved_qty AS available_qty FROM inventory_balance WHERE sku = :sku FOR UPDATE;

operations.label: UPDATE reserved quantity
operations.statement: UPDATE inventory_balance SET reserved_qty = reserved_qty + :quantity WHERE sku = :sku AND on_hand_qty - reserved_qty >= :quantity;

operations.label: INSERT stock hold
operations.statement: INSERT INTO stock_hold (id, cart_id, sku, quantity, expires_at, status) VALUES (:holdId, :cartId, :sku, :quantity, :expiresAt, 'active');

operations.label: SELECT live stock hold
operations.statement: SELECT id, expires_at, status FROM stock_hold WHERE id = :holdId;

operations.label: UPDATE hold consumed
operations.statement: UPDATE stock_hold SET status = 'consumed' WHERE id = :holdId AND status = 'active' AND expires_at > now();

operations.label: UPDATE sold stock counters
operations.statement: UPDATE inventory_balance SET on_hand_qty = on_hand_qty - :quantity, reserved_qty = reserved_qty - :quantity WHERE sku = :sku;
operations.description: Assumed transaction decrements counters only after an active hold is successfully consumed.

scenarios.title: Two bottles, first payment accepted
scenarios.description: Synthetic proposed recording. Noor opens cart-201, increases the bottle quantity from one to two, and checks out for EUR 49.00. Assume Inventory accepts a five-minute hold before payment authorization. Target contracts and instrumentation are assumptions; missing fields identify work still requiring a decision. The order commits, SNS delivers the receipt event to SQS, and Lambda submits the receipt before Noor opens confirmation. Email acceptance does not establish inbox arrival. Local review explicitly maps no Wiring elements.

occurrences.narration: The storefront reads the existing one-bottle basket. Capturing it introduces cart-201 into this recording; it does not mean the basket was created by this read.
occurrences.changeSummary: The existing basket becomes captured; no business state changes.

occurrences.narration: The Cart API uses the illustrative pricing library and persists two bottles at 2450 cents each. Editing the basket does not hold stock.
Noor reviews the already displayed EUR 49.00 total. This recorded human pause explicitly maps no Wiring elements. It is not a claim that the browser ceased to exist.
The checkout submission requests two units from Inventory. Inventory accepts hold hold-201 for five minutes, so authorization can proceed.
DemoPay authorizes 4900 cents for the first attempt. This is a recorded authorization result, not evidence of settlement or receipt delivery.

Checkout invokes its internal completion capability and commits paid order order-201. The self-connection describes an internal handoff, not another deployed service. The stock hold is consumed by this assumed completion responsibility.

Checkout publishes a paid-order event to SNS, and the assumed raw subscription delivers it to SQS. The worker and email provider are later in the recording; publication and fan-out alone do not establish consumption at this step.
The worker consumes the event, submits a receipt to DemoMail, and stores the accepted result. No browser action is mapped here even though the cart remains in the snapshot.

Noor opens the confirmation screen, which reads the accepted order summary through the Cart API. This synthetic request is an authored assumption. The confirmation read maps its own wire independently of the basket-screen read.

scenarios.title: A stale basket exceeds available stock
scenarios.description: Synthetic recording. Imani increases cart-202 from one bottle to three for EUR 73.50. Assume only two units remain when checkout requests a stock hold. Inventory rejects the request atomically, and the UI explains that quantity must change. No payment attempt or order is created. The recording stops at this feedback; it does not predict the shopper's next action.

occurrences.narration: The browser reads a previously saved one-bottle basket. No stock is reserved by this read.
The Cart API prices and saves three bottles. Basket edits do not guarantee availability at checkout, so the displayed EUR 73.50 total can coexist with insufficient stock.
Imani pauses before submitting the three-bottle basket. The author explicitly maps no Wiring elements for this human review.
Inventory finds two units available against a request for three and rejects the hold. Checkout stops before calling DemoPay. The basket stays editable and its reservation remains null.

The checkout screen explains that only two bottles are available. This visit maps the checkout screen displaying the recorded stock rejection. Payment, queue, and receipt elements remain outside this scenario's mapped scope.

scenarios.title: A different payment method succeeds
scenarios.description: Synthetic recording. Ellis checks out the existing two-bottle cart-203 for EUR 49.00. Assume hold-203 remains valid throughout the retry. The first payment is declined for insufficient funds; Ellis chooses another tokenized method. Checkout inspects the same hold, authorizes a new attempt, and commits one order. Both payment attempts remain captured. Wiring mapping is intentionally not recorded for retry-second-review; every other occurrence has an explicit mapping.

occurrences.narration: The storefront reads the existing two-bottle basket. The pricing library is outside this scenario's mapped scope because this recording makes no quantity change or repricing call.
Ellis reviews the checkout screen and selects the first saved payment method. Only the screen is mapped for this visit; its owner becomes relevant without implying a checkout submission yet.
Inventory accepts hold-203 for two bottles. This first visit creates the hold; the later visit to the same diagram node only checks it.
The first authorization returns insufficient_funds. The declined attempt is recorded and the stock hold remains live. No paid order exists at this point.
The checkout screen offers another tokenized method. The snapshot records no token or card data. Choosing the method does not yet invoke the retry endpoint.

Ellis reviews the retry choice. Wiring mapping was not recorded for this occurrence, so its missing mapping is different from an explicit empty mapping. Current Wiring emphasis clears here even though the previous visit mapped the checkout screen.

The retry endpoint checks hold-203 and finds it still valid. The existing hold is reused. This repeated reserve-node visit maps Inventory's get operation, not its reserve operation; the parallel check-reservation connection is independently relevant.

DemoPay authorizes a new 4900-cent attempt using the selected method. The first declined attempt remains captured. The two visits share a diagram node but map different payment connections and checkout operations.

Checkout's completion capability commits one paid order and consumes hold-203. The retry operation and completion operation are explicitly mapped; the first-attempt internal self-connection is not inferred for this visit.

Checkout publishes the committed order event to SNS, and the assumed subscription enqueues it in SQS. A declined attempt in the snapshot does not imply another gateway call. The receipt worker consumes the event at a later recorded step.
The receipt worker submits the paid order's receipt and records DemoMail acceptance. The two payment attempts remain business history, not Wiring usage inferred from their presence.

Ellis opens order confirmation after the receipt submission. This screen-only mapping does not infer Cart API participation. Rewinding to earlier visits recomputes their earlier/current/later emphasis without moving the shared Wiring geometry.

scenarios.title: Current: authorization without a hold
scenarios.description: Synthetic current-behavior recording. Assume Noor edits a one-bottle cart to two bottles for EUR 49.00. Checkout authorizes the payment without asking Inventory to hold stock. The recording stops at authorization and establishes neither stock availability nor order completion. Compare the proposed successful recording for the assumed stock-hold path. Current and Proposed are authored scenario labels, not computed Wiring versions.

occurrences.narration: The Angular basket screen reads the existing one-bottle cart. The SQL read introduces its captured state without reserving stock.
The quantity component calls the basket endpoint. The pricing library supplies EUR 49.00, and the assumed cart transaction updates line quantity, total, and version through separate SQL operations.
Noor reviews EUR 49.00 before submitting. This human pause has an explicit empty Wiring mapping.

Assume the current checkout path calls DemoPay directly and stores an authorized payment attempt. No Inventory call or stock write is recorded. The synthetic checkout trace labels the hold outcome unreserved. Authorization alone gives no assurance that both bottles remain available.
